Specifically, the Router noted the absence of the second dorsal fin (Barracouta have two; Pike have one rear-set dorsal), the wrong scale pattern (Pike have spots/blotches; Barracouta are silvery), and the lack of prominent fang-like teeth. The Router was not lenient; it correctly marked these major anatomical deviations as 'false'.

The visual evidence of finger fusion/indistinctness supports the Router's severity 3.0 rating over the expert's low-risk assessment. The background perspective distortion (1.5) is a valid minor artifact. The fine_grained_classifier failed to detect the species mismatch (predicting Barracouta with high confidence), demonstrating a limitation in handling out-of-distribution or visually similar but structurally distinct classes when the global shape (elongated fish) matches.
alignment_reasoning: Severe alignment failure. The image depicts a completely different species (Northern Pike) than the target class (Barracouta). The hands gripping the fish show fusion and lack of clear finger definition (Router severity 3.0), which is a common AI generation flaw in object interaction. The fish skin has a plastic/smooth texture lacking realistic scale granularity (severity 2.0). Background geometry shows slight warping. These defects prevent a higher artifact score despite the image being visually plausible at a glance.
